notes: Yamamoto-first discovery pass under the current durable repository authority. docs/PRIORITIES.md, docs/EDITORIAL.md, docs/DOMAINS.md, and radar/inbox/README.md were reread before research or grading. Fresh checks of Tsuyoshi Yamamoto, Jazz House ALFIE, BODY&SOUL, current Yamamoto schedule traces, Space M&A leads, and credible Japanese-jazz sources produced no additional verified unrecorded Yamamoto performance; September BODY&SOUL dates and the September 26 finale surfaced again but are already represented in canonical/curated/processed intake and were not duplicated. Stage 1 admits both Jazz in Hokutopia Vol.4 dates for event-specific reasons. September 25 is a three-part snapshot of the current Tokyo jazz scene centered on Shun Ishiwaka, culminating in Answer to Remember's explicit Miles Davis and John Coltrane centennial program. September 26 is Toninho Horta's first Japan visit in eight years and is structured uniquely as Horta solo, Horta with a Japan Jazz Collective, and Horta with a Japan Brazil Collective. Stage 2 assigns A+ to September 25 because the program is unusually strong and worth actively making room for, but the musicians and projects are active and the centennial concept does not create terminal scarcity. September 26 is assigned S only after a second scarcity challenge: Horta is a major living Brazilian guitar/composition voice returning to Japan after eight years, and the exact Tokyo three-part solo/Japan-jazz/Japan-Brazil sequence is not replicated by the other verified Japan-tour dates found in Osaka and Shizuoka. A+ would understate the genuine-regret-if-missed character of that specific Tokyo program; S+ is not warranted because Horta is playing multiple Japan dates and the event is not a farewell or final performance. Recent/current RADAR intake remains weighted toward A and A+, with S/S+ treated as scarce; this batch adds A+ 1, S 1, S+ 0 without using distribution as a quota.

en.why_it_matters: This is a compact map of the Tokyo jazz scene in motion. Shun Ishiwaka links three different ensemble languages across the evening, from the Yuya Wakai Trio to Marty Holoubek's guitar-bass-drums configuration and finally the larger Answer to Remember band, where the Miles Davis and John Coltrane centennials become material for a current Japanese ensemble rather than a museum tribute. The attraction is the sequence: the same rhythmic imagination keeps changing scale, instrumentation, and historical reference.
en.trip_verdict: If September overlaps with Tokyo, actively make room for the evening and treat Oji as the destination rather than an add-on after another plan. It is strong enough to build the night around, while the active musicians and projects leave room to protect truly scarcer one-offs elsewhere in Kanto.

es.why_it_matters: La noche funciona como un mapa compacto del jazz de Tokio en movimiento. Shun Ishiwaka conecta tres lenguajes de ensamble distintos: del trío de Yuya Wakai pasa a la configuración guitarra-bajo-batería de Marty Holoubek y termina en la formación más amplia de Answer to Remember, donde los centenarios de Miles Davis y John Coltrane sirven como materia para una banda japonesa actual y no como homenaje de museo. El atractivo está en la secuencia: una misma imaginación rítmica cambia de escala, instrumentación y referencia histórica durante la noche.
es.trip_verdict: Si septiembre coincide con Tokio, sí le haría espacio activamente y tomaría Oji como destino de la noche, no como complemento de otro plan. Da para construir la velada alrededor del concierto, pero la actividad continua de estos músicos deja margen para reservar las decisiones más drásticas para one-offs realmente más escasos en Kanto.

en.why_it_matters: Horta's return is compelling because Tokyo is not getting a generic tour set. After eight years away from Japan, he moves through three frames in one afternoon: guitar and voice alone, then a current Japanese jazz group, then a Japan-Brazil ensemble that puts flute, voices, two guitars, electric bass, and drums around his harmonic language. The program turns a living Minas Gerais master into an actual exchange with musicians working in Japan now.
en.trip_verdict: If you are in Tokyo or can reach it comfortably from Kanto, protect the afternoon and build the day around Oji. The Osaka and Shizuoka dates provide other ways to hear Horta on this Japan visit, but they do not duplicate this exact three-part Tokyo program.

es.why_it_matters: Lo especial del regreso de Horta es que Tokio no recibe una parada genérica de gira. Después de ocho años sin tocar en Japón, pasa por tres marcos en una sola tarde: primero guitarra y voz a solas, luego un colectivo de jazz japonés actual y finalmente un ensamble Japón-Brasil que coloca flauta, voces, dos guitarras, bajo eléctrico y batería alrededor de su lenguaje armónico. El programa convierte la visita de un maestro vivo de Minas Gerais en un intercambio real con músicos que hoy trabajan en Japón.
es.trip_verdict: Si estás en Tokio o puedes llegar cómodamente desde Kanto, protegería la tarde y armaría el día alrededor de Oji. Las fechas de Osaka y Shizuoka ofrecen otras maneras de escuchar a Horta durante esta visita a Japón, pero no repiten este programa tokiota de tres partes.

priority_review.rationale: Concrete scarcity: authorized ticketing identifies this as Toninho Horta's first Japan visit in eight years, and the Tokyo date uniquely sequences Horta solo, a Japan Jazz Collective, and a Japan Brazil Collective with two distinct Japan-based lineups. Other verified Japan-tour stops exist—Billboard Live Osaka with Lisa Ono on September 29 and a Shizuoka solo show on September 30—so the review does not claim the visit itself is one-night-only. The second editorial challenge asked whether A+ would still capture the recommendation; for this exact Tokyo program, it would understate the genuine regret of missing a major living Brazilian guitar/composition voice in a rare, locally assembled cross-cultural context after an eight-year absence. S+ is not warranted because the tour has multiple Japan dates and this is neither a farewell nor a final performance.
